title: Abstract

nodes.title: Abstract (intro)
nodes.summary: Introduces a 2015 PLOS ONE article reporting new archaeological excavations at Monte Verde, Chile. Stone artifacts, faunal remains, and burned areas indicate ephemeral human activity in a sandur plain setting, radiocarbon and luminescence dated to about 18,500 to 14,500 cal BP. Discusses debates on the timing, routes, and dispersal of the initial peopling of the Americas, site validity criteria, and North versus South American colonization. Also covers the author affiliations, funding sources, and competing-interest statement.

nodes.title: Introduction
nodes.summary: The text introduces debate on the initial peopling of the Americas, covering arrival timing (at or before 15,000 years ago), migration routes via Beringia, and the discredited Clovis-first model. It contrasts two explanations for South American stone tools: diffusion of Clovis-derived Fishtail points versus independent adaptation from an East Asian source, citing sites like Monte Verde II, Gault, Cactus Hill, and Paisley Cave. It then describes new Monte Verde and Chinchihuapi excavations in Chile revealing ephemeral human activity dated ~14,500 to possibly 19,000 cal BP, previous findings at MV-I and MV-II, geological context, and research objectives and methods.

nodes.title: Materials and Methods
nodes.summary: Describes the 2013 field methods at Monte Verde and Chinchihuapi Creek sites in Chile: cores, test pits, and excavation blocks, plus 39 lithics and 12 burned features recovered, suggesting intermittent human presence. Covers the geomorphology and stratigraphy: glacial outwash history, braided drainage, paleoenvironment (pollen-based vegetation shifts), SCH-Fm sedimentary facies and dating, and the tephra lenses that hold the cultural horizons. Discusses site intactness, lack of taphonomic disturbance, and in situ burned features with embedded lithics and bone.

nodes.title: Chronology
nodes.summary: Describes the chronology of the Monte Verde, Chile sites (MV-I, MV-II/CH-I) using 14C and OSL dating. Nine radiocarbon dates from burned features and charcoal are reported, with stratigraphic agreement to prior dates, ranging roughly 10,600 to 19,500 cal BP for cultural levels and 14,000 to 15,000 cal BP for the MV-II occupation. Failed dating attempts, dubious deeper charcoal (~22,000-23,500 cal BP), and older non-cultural peat dates (up to ~43,500 BP) are discussed. Charcoal derives from Nothofagus; OSL methods, sediment description, and sequence results are covered. Conservative occupation estimate: ~19,000-14,000 cal BP.

nodes.title: Material Remains
Lithic assemblages
nodes.summary: Describes lithic assemblages from Monte Verde (Chile), totaling 39 stones, dated across several phases from ~25,000 to ~10,600 cal BP. Covers percussion-flaked local basalts, andesites, and exotic serpentine, quartz, quartzite, and limestone; expedient tool use and manuports; sling stones, choppers, wedges, and cores; intact, unweathered deposits; MV-II diversity and long-distance exchange; a Paijan-like projectile point and drill at CH-I; grinding stones with plant residues; and uncertain cultural status of deeper MV-I materials. Discusses pebble tool industries, unifacial versus bifacial technologies, and possible shared North American antecedents.

nodes.title: Burned features
nodes.summary: Describes twelve burned archaeological features at Monte Verde, Chile, dated ~14,000 to at least 18,500 cal BP, found mainly in site MV-I within stratum MV-7 and also in CH-I. Features lack clay-lined pits or burned rocks but contain animal bones, lithics, ash, and charcoal. Their size, thickness, and stratigraphic position are given, along with an exotic clay block with a percussion flake and uncertain origin. Notes that no other burned features were found and that it is unclear whether the features relate to the MV-II occupation or to separate visits.

nodes.title: Faunal remains
nodes.summary: Describes faunal remains: four burned, one scorched, and four unburned bone fragments (1–3.5 cm) from sites MV-I and CH-I, mostly too small to identify; likely ghomphothere or paleocamelid, with one tibia head possibly deer or small horse. Table 2 lists 2013 features by unit, dimensions, and contents (ash, charcoal, lithic, bone). Bones linked to burned features with stone artifacts and plant remains, suggesting human activity; no cutmarks. An animal skin from a peat ball at 2.1 m dated about 43,500 cal years ago, consistent with a prior 42,000 BP assay.

nodes.title: Paleobotany
nodes.summary: Paleobotany study of stratum MV-I and MV-II samples: flotation yielded only burned stems and wood charcoal. Pollen, starch, and phytolith analyses of five samples show probable food processing and local environment. Sample 3 (~15,680 cal BP) shows abundant Nothofagus and elevated Poaceae, indicating grass seed parching in a grassy wetland. Sample 4 (~18,578 cal BP) is Liguliflorae-dominated, indicating an open weedy area with trees. Grinding stones (~14,500 cal BP) show Polygonum and Rumex, suggesting seed, nut, and edible plant processing. Diatoms and sponge spicules suggest drier summer use after 15,000 cal BP.

Material Remains at Monte Verde (Chile): 39 lithic artifacts (~25,000–10,600 cal BP) of local basalts, andesites and exotic stones, incl. sling stones, choppers, cores, a Paijan-like point and grinding stones with plant residues; twelve burned features (~14,000–18,500 cal BP) with bones, ash and charcoal, one exotic clay block; faunal remains (mostly unidentifiable, possibly ghomphothere or paleocamelid, one animal skin ~43,500 cal years ago); paleobotany showing grass seed parching, edible plant processing and drier summer use after 15,000 cal BP.

nodes.title: Discussion
nodes.summary: Describes Monte Verde, Chile archaeology: paleoclimate warming and cooling events (~26,000-15,000 cal BP) matching low-density, short-term hunting, gathering, and stone-tool horizons at several sites. Notes volcanic ash and ecological barriers affecting mobility, exotic stone materials indicating mobility or exchange, and a later prolonged settlement at MV-II after ~15,000 cal BP with varied resources. Proposes exchange networks by ~14,500 cal BP and compares the record to Nunamiut and high-latitude analogues.

nodes.title: Conclusion
nodes.summary: Conclusion of a Monte Verde (Chile) archaeology paper: human presence ~18,500-14,500 cal BP likely linked to Pacific coast and Andean passes to Argentina, evidenced by exotic lithics and coastal plants. Discontinuous, ephemeral horizons are hard to trace beyond ~8-10 m2; larger excavations would likely show similar patterns. Early sites (MV-II, MV-I, CH-I/II) are reassessed, and low-visibility early records in Brazil, Peru and North America challenge assumptions. Concludes most evidence supports arrival about 20,000-15,000 years ago, with the early record being unpredictable and complex.

nodes.title: Supporting Information
nodes.summary: Supporting information for a Monte Verde (Chile) archaeology paper: S1 Fig describes a modern low-energy drainage setting near Tronador volcano resembling the buried sandur plain; S2 Fig gives schematic stratigraphic profiles and OSL dates of Units 45(A) and MV-II, outlining Phases I-V of erosion, deposition, creek formation (~15,000 yrs ago), and burial by strata MV-1 to MV-5; S3 Fig shows thin orange tephra lenses and a flaked tool embedded in one; S4 Fig shows features with underlying tephra and burned areas; S5 Fig shows a fractured, partly burned animal tibia epiphysis; S1 File lists lithics, chronology, mineral, micromorphological, magnetic, pollen/phytolith, luminescence dating, and usewear texts; acknowledgments and author contributions close the text.

nodes.title: Monte Verde Tephra Strata, Figures, Supplements, Acknowledgments, and Author Contributions
nodes.summary: Describes stratigraphic phases IV and V at Monte Verde (strata MV-1 to MV-7, soils, and the MV-II occupation at ~42,223 years). Covers supplementary figures on thin orange tephra lenses and micro-settings, archaeological features (clay object, Feature 9 with tephra, burned area, flake), and a partially burned animal tibia epiphysis dated 13,940–13,560 cal BP. Lists S1 File text sections A–H (lithics, chronostratigraphy, mineralogy, micromorphology, magnetism, pollen/phytolith/starch, luminescence dating, usewear). Acknowledges field helpers, illustrator, foundation, landowner, and reviewers. Lists author contributions by task.

summary: A 2015 PLOS ONE paper reports 2013 excavations at Monte Verde and Chinchihuapi Creek, Chile, finding ephemeral human activity on a sandur plain dated about 18,500 to 14,500 cal BP. Covers debates on the peopling of the Americas (timing, Beringia routes, Clovis-first, Fishtail diffusion versus independent origin), field methods, geomorphology, radiocarbon and OSL chronology, lithics, burned features, faunal and paleobotanical remains, paleoclimate context, exchange networks, and supplementary materials.

title: References
summary: This text is the reference list (items 1–53) from the PLOS ONE article 'New Archaeological Evidence from Monte Verde, Chile' (November 2015). It cites works on the peopling of the Americas, Paleoamerican sites (Paisley Caves, Buttermilk Creek, Cactus Hill, Pedra Furada, Toca da Tira Peia), Monte Verde volumes and reports, geology, pollen, chronology and radiocarbon/luminescence dating, lithic analysis, genetics, cranial morphology, and Peruvian and Argentine archaeology.
